findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn1 (up)
findings.evidence: 184.3 ms per step against an ideal 9.2 ms (5% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 4052 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Dtype and copy kernels take a large share
findings.evidence: 23% of device time is casts and copies
findings.lever: find the modules issuing `.to(dtype)` round trips (autocast boundaries, adapter branches) and keep one dtype through them

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn2 (up)
findings.evidence: 169.7 ms per step against an ideal 9.2 ms (5% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 4052 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Many small memory-bound kernels
findings.evidence: 43% of device time (17369 calls per step) is elementwise, normalisation, copy, memory and reduction work
findings.lever: fusion (fewer, larger kernels): norm + modulation, activation + multiply, cast + matmul input; half the time is the most a fusion usually recovers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: linear attn1.to_q (up)
findings.evidence: 142.9 ms per step against an ideal 3.5 ms (2% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 4052 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: linear attn2.to_out (up)
findings.evidence: 142.5 ms per step against an ideal 3.5 ms (2% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 4052 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn1 (down)
findings.evidence: 144.6 ms per step against an ideal 6.1 ms (4% efficient, compute-bound), 24 layers; all rated pieces together leave 4052 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Some steps in the window were much slower than the rest
findings.evidence: 1 step(s) took over twice the median: step 20 (2, 68, 92) 5071 ms
findings.lever: a latent shape seen for the first time costs kernel and primitive creation (seconds); fewer distinct shapes (buckets.max_shapes) and a longer warm-up
